BUS.G11.T2.CREATIVE.A1.title: Creative thinking & problem-solving (advanced)
BUS.G11.T2.CREATIVE.A1.description: Applying creative thinking to business problems: routine vs creative thinking, mental blocks, techniques (brainstorming, mind-mapping, Delphi, force-field analysis), working with others, and conventional vs non-conventional (including indigenous) solutions checked against reality.
BUS.G11.T2.CREATIVE.A1.strand: T2 — Creative thinking, stress & change, action plans, setting up, ethics & presentation
BUS.G11.T2.CREATIVE.A1.recovery_strategy: Routine thinking follows known steps; creative thinking breaks the pattern to find new ideas. Mental blocks (fear of failure, assuming one right answer) stop creativity. Techniques such as brainstorming, mind-mapping, Delphi and force-field analysis help generate and weigh options.

questions.question: What best describes creative thinking, compared with routine thinking?
options: Generating new ideas by breaking away from the usual pattern
Repeating the same fixed steps every time
Doing exactly what a manual says
questions.expected: Generating new ideas by breaking away from the usual pattern
questions.memo: Creative thinking produces fresh ideas by departing from habit; routine thinking simply follows familiar, fixed steps.

questions.question: Something that stops a person from thinking creatively is called a _________ block.
questions.expected: mental
questions.memo: A mental block — such as fear of failure or assuming there is only one right answer — prevents creative thinking.

questions.question: True or false: In brainstorming, ideas are generated freely at first without being judged.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Brainstorming encourages many ideas without early judgement, so people feel free to contribute; evaluation comes later.

questions.question: Which of these is a creative-thinking technique?
questions.expected: Mind-mapping
questions.memo: Mind-mapping is a creative-thinking technique that visually links ideas around a central topic.

questions.question: The _________ technique gathers expert opinions in rounds, without the experts meeting face to face.
questions.expected: Delphi
questions.memo: The Delphi technique collects and refines expert views over several rounds without the experts meeting, reducing the influence of dominant personalities.

questions.question: True or false: Creative thinking can help a business improve the way it works.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Creative thinking generates new solutions and improvements, helping a business solve problems and work better.

questions.question: Sort each example into routine thinking or creative thinking.

items.text: Following the same daily checklist without change
Combining two unrelated ideas to invent a new product
Processing invoices the usual way
Brainstorming fresh ways to reach customers
Re-ordering stock exactly as always
Finding an unconventional use for a waste material

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Following fixed steps is routine; generating new ideas, combinations and unconventional uses is creative thinking.

questions.question: Which of these is a mental block to creativity?
options: Assuming there is only one right answer to a problem
Asking 'what if we tried something different?'
Listening to many points of view
questions.expected: Assuming there is only one right answer to a problem
questions.memo: Assuming a single right answer shuts down new ideas — a classic mental block. The other options open up creative thinking.

questions.question: Put the steps of generating and using a creative solution in the correct order.

items.text: Define the problem clearly
Generate many ideas freely
Evaluate the ideas against the real situation
Choose and implement the best idea

questions.expected: define, generate, evaluate, implement
questions.memo: First understand the problem, then generate ideas freely, then judge them against reality, and finally implement the best one.

questions.question: _________-field analysis weighs the forces pushing for a change against the forces resisting it.
questions.expected: Force
questions.memo: Force-field analysis lists the driving forces for a change and the restraining forces against it, to decide whether and how to proceed.

questions.question: What is a benefit of working with others to generate ideas?
options: A wider range of ideas and perspectives is produced
Only one person's view is ever heard
It removes the need to evaluate ideas
questions.expected: A wider range of ideas and perspectives is produced
questions.memo: Different people bring different experiences, so working together produces more varied ideas than thinking alone.

questions.question: What is the difference between a conventional and a non-conventional solution?
options: A conventional solution is the usual, expected one; a non-conventional solution is new or unusual
A conventional solution is always wrong
A non-conventional solution is the one in the textbook
There is no difference between them
questions.expected: A conventional solution is the usual, expected one; a non-conventional solution is new or unusual
questions.memo: Conventional solutions follow the normal approach; non-conventional (including indigenous) solutions take a fresh, less obvious route.

questions.question: Sort each item into whether it is a creative-thinking technique or not.

items.text: Brainstorming
Ignoring the problem and hoping it goes away
Mind-mapping
Copying a competitor's product exactly
The Delphi technique
Force-field analysis

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Brainstorming, mind-mapping, Delphi and force-field analysis are techniques. Ignoring a problem or copying others is not creative thinking.

questions.question: How can indigenous knowledge help a business solve a problem?
options: It offers local, traditional knowledge that can suggest practical solutions
It must never be used in business
It only works for very large companies
It always costs more than other methods
questions.expected: It offers local, traditional knowledge that can suggest practical solutions
questions.memo: Indigenous knowledge draws on local, traditional experience and can provide creative, context-appropriate solutions.

questions.question: True or false: Even a clever creative idea should be checked against the reality of the business before it is used.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Creative ideas must be tested against the business's real resources, costs and conditions to make sure they can actually work.

questions.question: A manager says, 'We have always done it this way, so there is no other option.' Which mental block is this?
options: Sticking to habit and assuming only one right answer
Being too open to new ideas
questions.expected: Sticking to habit and assuming only one right answer
questions.memo: Relying on 'how it has always been done' is a mental block that blocks new ideas.

questions.question: Faced with a brand-new problem no procedure covers, why is creative thinking more useful than routine thinking?
options: A new problem has no ready-made answer, so fresh ideas are needed
Routine thinking always solves new problems instantly
Creative thinking avoids solving the problem
New problems never need any thinking
questions.expected: A new problem has no ready-made answer, so fresh ideas are needed
questions.memo: Routine thinking only repeats known steps. A genuinely new problem needs creative thinking to generate solutions that do not yet exist.

questions.question: Put the steps of running a force-field analysis in a sensible order.

items.text: State the change being considered
List the forces driving the change
List the forces resisting the change
Weigh the forces and decide how to proceed

questions.expected: change, driving, restraining, decide
questions.memo: Name the change, list the forces for it, list the forces against it, then weigh them up to decide.

questions.question: Why is it important to assess a creative solution against the reality of the business environment?
options: So that the idea actually fits the business's resources, costs and conditions
So that the idea can be as expensive as possible
So that no idea is ever used
So that only the oldest idea wins
questions.expected: So that the idea actually fits the business's resources, costs and conditions
questions.memo: An idea is only useful if the business can realistically afford and implement it, so creative solutions are checked against the real situation.

questions.question: A bakery has surplus bread it cannot sell by closing time. Which response shows the most creative thinking?
options: Partnering with a shelter to turn surplus bread into a low-cost evening meal range
Throwing all the surplus away as usual
Refusing to consider any new idea
questions.expected: Partnering with a shelter to turn surplus bread into a low-cost evening meal range
questions.memo: Turning a waste problem into a new offering through a partnership is a creative, non-conventional solution that also adds value.
